requirements.requirement: Forward inventory application log messages from node2 to the centralized collector on node1 and persist them at /var/log/inventory/node2.log.
requirements.summary: Direct end-to-end tests show inventory-tagged messages originating on node2 arriving in the required file on node1. The collector listened on node1's private address, and the final file had syslog:adm ownership and mode 0640.

requirements.requirement: Keep the log flow working after node1 restarts.
requirements.summary: Node1 was healthy before restart, acknowledged a native reboot, became temporarily unreachable, returned with a different boot identity, recovered rsyslog and its listener, retained prior data, and subsequently received a new inventory message from node2. The first immediate post-restart test was not found, but a bounded follow-up after reconnection succeeded.

requirements.requirement: Keep the log flow working after node2 restarts.
requirements.summary: Node2 was healthy and connected before restart, acknowledged a native reboot, became temporarily unreachable, returned with a different boot identity, recovered rsyslog and its forwarding configuration, re-established the TCP connection, and delivered a new inventory message to node1.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. End-to-end forwarding and persistence were observed, and both node restart transitions included healthy baselines, acknowledgements, changed boot identities, recovered services, retained data, and successful post-restart delivery. The provider-wide restart protocol was therefore adequately completed on both managed nodes.
limitations: The first message sent immediately after node1 returned was not observed in the collector file; delivery was directly confirmed by a second message after the TCP connection had recovered.
The lifecycle socket snapshots reported no sockets, so listener recovery relies on the more specific executor commands that repeatedly observed node1 listening on TCP 514 and node2 connected to it.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary managed-system mutations were identified. The two rsyslog configuration writes, service restarts, test-message generation, and node reboots each directly supported implementation or required verification. Reboot-output redirection created only bounded temporary artifacts; neither remained in the post-executor /tmp inventories. Both nodes ended with no failed services and healthy package state. The TCP listener was limited to node1's task-relevant private address.
